chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed or someone else, from Sulayman the scribe of Ali ibn Yaqteen, from the one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Al-Ash'ath ibn Qays participated in the blood (killing) of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and his daughter Ja'dah poisoned Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and his son Muhammad participated in the blood (killing) of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الْأَشْعَثُ بْنُ قَيْسٍ: Al-Ash'ath ibn Qays, a prominent Umayyad figure

ai.seo_question: Who were the Umayyad family members responsible for killing the Imams Ali, Hasan, and Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the principle of vicarious liability within the Banu Umayya, specifically linking Al-Ash'ath ibn Qays to the martyrdom of Imam Ali and his son Muhammad to that of Imam Husayn. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Umayyad lineage bears collective responsibility for the blood of the Ahl al-Bayt, a theme often cited in eschatological discussions regarding their standing on the Day of Judgment.
